subject: Surgical micropatch scheduling + network guardrails for Private deployment

From: Mateo Alvarez <mateo_alvarez@redwood.ai>

Cc: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: 2025-06-12T09:10:00-07:00
Subject: Surgical micropatch scheduling + network guardrails for Private deployment

Tom —

We ran the preflight on your private fleet last week and I want to propose a surgical micropatch plan that minimizes churn while keeping rollback fast. High level: we will apply a point patch (1.7.3 -> 1.7.4) to the control-plane helpers and a small runtime fix to the host agent. No DB schema changes.

Key notes and asks:
- Window options: preferred slice is 2025-06-25 01:00–03:00 UTC (low traffic). Alternate: 2025-06-26 same window. Please confirm which works for your change control.
- Version pinning: we will pin the fleet to the outgoing stable manifest before the patch (manifest v2 snapshot attached) so we can fully revert to 1.7.3 if needed. Pinning will be applied at the deployment-controller level and recorded in the audit log.
- Canary & rollout: 5% canary hosts first (control-plane + host-agent), 30-minute health watch, then 25% -> 100% if metrics look good.
- Safety gates: P95 latency <= baseline + 15%, error-rate delta <= 0.5% absolute. If either gate trips we trigger automated rollback.
- KV cache handling: we will perform a coordinated KV-cache soft-flush on canary hosts to avoid cache poisoning, with prefix-based warm-up post-patch.
- Network guardrails and draining: network cordon + graceful drain on canary nodes, BGP withdraw on the last tranche only if we need to force-evacuate. Karthik, can you draft the exact cordon sequence and short net commands?
- Rollback & RTO: automated rollback script targets a sub-10 minute RTO (snapshot restore for control-plane binaries + re-pin). Manual rollback checklist included in attached PDF.

Attachments: patch_manifest_v2.xlsx (manifest and file checksums), network-drain-checklist.pdf (drain order & contacts).

Operational notes for Orchid SRE: we need a primary SRE contact on-call during the window and permission for a single emergency warm-standby failover if necessary. Also please open an RFC and share the ID so we can annotate it in the runbook.

Next steps: please confirm the preferred window and SRE contact. Once we have that I will schedule internal dry-run rehearsal and send the final runbook.

Thanks,
Mateo
Mateo Alvarez
Senior Solutions Engineer — Private Deployments
Redwood Inference

- We prefer 2025-06-25 01:00–03:00 UTC. That aligns with our change-window.
- SLA impact: we need confirmation on customer-facing token-gen latency; our requirement is that any maintenance must not push P95 token latency by more than 25% for longer than 5 minutes. Your 15% gate sounds conservative which is good — can you confirm the escalation if we see a 20% spike for 3 minutes (i.e., do we pause, roll back, or continue)?
- RTO: sub-10m is acceptable but we need an explicit statement of what 'automated rollback' will restore (binaries, pins, config).

I will create RFC-ORCH-4521 in our change system and assign SRE on-call (sre@orchidhealth.com).

Tom — thanks for confirming the preferred slot and for opening RFC-ORCH-4521. Quick clarifications and commitments: 

- Escalation / gate behavior: if P95 token latency spikes between 15–25% for under 5 minutes we will pause the rollout and investigate (no automatic promotion). If any gate is breached beyond the stated threshold or persists >5 minutes we execute automated rollback. If rollback fails we trigger manual failover to a warm standby pinned to 1.7.3 (manual RTO 15–30m).
- Automated rollback scope: binaries (control-plane and agent), deployment-controller pin toggled back to 1.7.3, and an optional KV-cache re-seed step. Config and preserved state (persistent volumes) are not touched.
- Canary step detail: canary group = dedicated control-plane helpers + two host-agent replicas; drain and soft-flush KV cache before patch. Post-patch warm-up uses the prior prefix warmers for 20 minutes.

Internal action items (Irene/Karthik): please produce
1) a one-page runbook section with explicit commands for KV soft-flush + re-seed (Irene),
2) network cordon + BGP withdraw script and netflow sampling preflight (Karthik).

I’ll run a dry-run in our staging environment on 6/20 and attach the rehearsal notes to the runbook.

Mateo

Putting the network guardrail draft here (brief):

Preflight (T-72h):
- netflow sampling on ingress (5 min baseline) + packet loss scan across all vlan trunks; capture to s3-staging.
- validate BGP RIBs on edge routers, stash current routes (bgp show ip route > /tmp/bgp-before).

T-30m (immediately before drain):
- set lb drain timeout = 10s; verify sticky session cookies TTL >= 60s.
- cordon nodes by marking node.metric.maintenance=true on the controller (example: curl -XPOST /api/node/cordon?id=X).

Canary drain sequence (script in repo: net_guardrails.sh):
1) soft-drain host-agent processes (systemctl stop redwood-agent --signal=SIGTERM; wait 15s)
2) run KV soft-flush (redis: SCRIPT flush_prefix 'orch:' 'grace=30s')
3) check application health endpoints (/_health) for 3 consecutive 10s checks before marking patch complete for tranche.

If we need to evacuate a tranche quickly:
- withdraw BGP for the tranche VLANs (sudo bgpctl withdraw <prefix-list>)
- scale up warm standby in the pinned pool and shift 100% traffic there via LB override.

Rollback helper commands (automated):
- restore manifest: /opt/redwood/scripts/restore_manifest.sh --snapshot=manifest-v2
- restart control-plane (systemctl restart redwood-control --no-block)

I attached net_guardrails.sh to the runbook. I'll add concrete command examples and test outputs after the rehearsal.

-Karthik
